pathway.title: Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Deleveraging is earnings-led and has further to run only if earnings hold. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025 and reported EBITDA 54.85% above it, while carrying debt barely moved, so net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 4.70x to 2.92x. The creditor consequence is that the improvement is exposed to any fall in occupancy or price, not locked in by repayment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C01

Interest cover is the tightest metric. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x and Adjusted EBITDA 2.52x, and on the 7.00% coupon alone reported EBITDA covers interest 2.83x. The mechanical break-even is large, a 34.51% fall in reported EBITDA before it equals cash interest plus capital spending, but the same earnings reverting to the FY2025 level would put cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C15; calculation C04; calculation C03

Liquidity is adequate in size but deposit-funded. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 330,249 thousand compare with unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand, and unrestricted cash is 63.68% of them. Even if every implied cancellable deposit were refunded at once, cash would be USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so the exposure is the speed of deposit reversal, not its size. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand, held as escrow and card-processor reserves, is excluded from the cash used here. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01; calculation C05

Refinancing risk is remote before 2030 but unverified after it. The only principal is the 7.00% notes due September 2030, with the revolver ending in August 2030, and the issuer estimates the debt's fair value at 96.04% of principal. Both facilities limit added debt and restricted payments and the issuer reports compliance, but the indenture, credit agreement, guarantors and covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom to add debt or pay out cash is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C16

The business has two real concentrations: a brand license and permits. The National Geographic license runs to 2040 but National Geographic can end it early on a change of control, and Galápagos permits run on 20-year terms that can end early for non-compliance. A sale of the company would therefore trigger a credit question that the supplied debt documents cannot answer. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 54

Financial policy is neutral to supportive but cash is going to growth. No dividends were paid, the preferred stock converted, and the 2025 refinancing extended maturities, yet cash purchases of businesses and minority interests used 56.31% of free cash flow from FY2024 to September 2026, and put options remain outstanding. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

cells.text: Expedition cruises on owned small ships and land-based adventure travel under eight brands: Lindblad Expeditions, Natural Habitat, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine, Classic Journeys, the Thomson Group safari and trek brands, White Desert and Echo Charlie
Many small-group products reduce reliance on one itinerary but each runs in remote places with limited infrastructure
Lindblad segment: ship-based expeditions. Land Experiences: land-based tours, safaris and treks. Share of FY2025 tour revenues 64.28% and 35.72%
Ship economics drive two thirds of revenue and Adjusted EBITDA
12 owned expedition ships and 10 seasonal chartered vessels; two owned ships built 1981 and 1982 retire in October 2026; a river ship charter starts in 2027
Owned ships are the collateral base; retirements and charters change capacity and fixed commitments
Premium list pricing, little discounting; deposit at booking, balance 60 to 120 days before departure; guests book about nine months ahead
Revenue visibility and a customer-deposit float that funds operations
Direct channel 68% and agents 32% of expedition guest ticket revenue in FY2025; about 90% of expedition guest ticket revenue from U.S. guests
Reliance on U.S. demand and on direct marketing spend
Lindblad ticket revenue is larger in the first and third quarters; drydocks fall in the second and fourth quarters; land brands peak in the second to fourth quarters by brand
Quarterly earnings and cash are uneven; twelve-month measures are needed
National Geographic brand license through 2040 with termination rights; WWF license for Natural Habitat through 2028; Galápagos permits on 20-year contracts
A lost license or permit removes demand or capacity
Four U.S.-flagged vessels are subject to the Coastwise Laws; U.S. embarkations require passenger-deposit escrow certified by the Federal Maritime Commission
Ownership limits constrain equity raising; escrow ties up cash
Largest operating costs are ship maintenance, payroll, fuel, food and beverage, travel agent services and marketing; royalties sit in selling and marketing
Fuel and the royalty step-up raise costs ahead of EBITDA
Purchases of property and equipment were USD 47.7 million in FY2025, mainly vessel improvements
Maintenance and refurbishment are recurring cash needs

runs.text: Strength, ranked first: the earnings base has moved a long way. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025, Lindblad segment occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026 against 78% in FY2024, and net leverage is 2.92x on reported EBITDA. In FY2025 the segment turned each extra dollar of revenue into 28.17% of Adjusted EBITDA against an average margin of 16.10%, so price and occupancy gains reach EBITDA quickly and lower leverage without repayment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07

Strength, ranked second: the maturity wall is distant and the creditor group is secured. The 7.00% notes and the revolver are due in 2030 and share first-priority liens on substantially all assets, so there is no principal to refinance for almost four years and the secured claim sits over the ship fleet. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11

Strength, ranked third: cash generation is positive after capital spending. Free cash flow was USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months and 14.44% of carrying debt, which supports gradual debt reduction if acquisitions slow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C09

Weakness, ranked first: cover is thin for a discretionary, season-dependent business. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x, and cover was 1.70x in FY2025, so a moderate earnings fall quickly absorbs the margin of safety. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03

Weakness, ranked second: liquidity depends on customer deposits and is not covenant-tested here. Unrestricted cash is 63.68% of unearned passenger revenues and the revolver is undrawn but unread, so a booking shock would draw cash before revenue falls. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C05

Weakness, ranked third: dependence on a brand license and permits, with control and covenant facts missing. The license can end on a change of control, the Galápagos permits can end early, and the proxy statement and debt documents are not supplied, so the creditor cannot see who controls the company or what it may pay out. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only new debt in the period supplied is the USD 675.0 million of 7.00% senior secured notes due September 2030, issued on 2025-08-20 to prepay the 6.75% and 9.00% notes and to extend the USD 60.0 million revolver to August 2030. No new debt was issued in the first nine months of 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11

The 2026 transactions were funded from cash: 60% of White Desert and Echo Charlie for USD 66.6 million on 2026-09-14, with the remaining 40.0% subject to put and call options, and additional stakes in Natural Habitat and Classic Journeys for USD 16.6 million and USD 3.2 million. The preferred stock was converted into common stock on 2026-02-03. A related-party acquisition, Terra & Tu, carries a future payment of up to USD 4.0 million whose date and amount paid are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.value: - Material: The indenture for the 7.00% senior secured notes due 2030, the collateral trust agreement and the revolving credit agreement with its amendments are listed as exhibits incorporated by reference and are not supplied. Fundamental credit can report what the issuer states but cannot measure covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity or guarantor coverage until the documents are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Total debt moved only from USD 621,825 thousand at the end of 2023 to USD 664,516 thousand at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 53,995 thousand in FY2023 to USD 133,642 thousand over the last twelve months. Gross leverage on reported EBITDA therefore fell from 11.52x to 8.54x, 7.68x and 4.97x, and net leverage from 8.61x to 2.92x; on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA the path is 8.73x to 4.57x gross and 6.53x to 2.68x net. Tour revenue grew 19.59% in FY2025 while cost of tours rose more slowly, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 12.50% in FY2023 to 16.93% over the last twelve months. The consequence for creditors is that deleveraging depends on occupancy and pricing holding, because the debt itself did not fall.

fields.value: Interest cover is the thinnest part of the picture. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 1.24x in FY2023, 1.70x in FY2025 and 2.32x over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA gives 2.52x. The last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 57,725 thousand still includes interest on the 6.75% and 9.00% notes repaid on 2025-08-20; the 7.00% coupon alone is USD 47,250 thousand a year, which reported EBITDA covers 2.83x. Cash interest paid in FY2025 exceeded interest expense, net, by USD 5,535 thousand and the annual report does not reconcile the two, so coverage is stated on cash paid. The notes pay interest on March 15 and September 15, so quarterly cash interest is lumpy.

fields.value: Cash generation is strong but partly deposit-funded. Free cash flow was USD 63,838 thousand in FY2025 and USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months, 71.82% of reported EBITDA. Growth in unearned passenger revenues supplied 35.41% of FY2025 operating cash flow and 30.90% over the last twelve months, and purchases of property and equipment fell 48.80% over nine months against a 2025 period that included refurbishing the vessels bought in 2025. Free cash flow covers the 2026 acquisitions but leaves little: after USD 54,604 thousand paid for businesses and USD 19,760 thousand for noncontrolling interests, the nine-month free cash flow of USD 92,510 thousand leaves USD 18,146 thousand. Deposits reverse if bookings slow, so reported free cash flow overstates the cash a downturn would leave.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate on the face of the balance sheet but depends on deposits. Unrestricted cash of USD 274,949 thousand plus USD 55.3 million of undrawn revolver is 49.70% of total debt, yet unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand are larger than cash, which equals 63.68% of them. The issuer counts a deposit as a contract liability only once the guest can no longer cancel for a full refund; contract liabilities were USD 275,234 thousand, which implies about USD 156,554 thousand of deposits still cancellable. The issuer states a working-capital deficit of USD 124.9 million. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand is escrow and card-processor reserves and is not counted. The mechanism is a seasonal float: cash rises as deposits are collected before voyages and falls as voyages are delivered, so a booking shock would drain cash before revenue falls.

fields.value: Debt structure is simple but not fully documented. One issue of USD 675.0 million of 7.00% senior secured notes falls due on 2030-09-15 and a USD 60.0 million revolver matures in August 2030, so no principal falls due before the third quarter of 2030 and refinancing risk is a 2030 event. Both are secured by first-priority pari passu liens on substantially all assets, with the Company and certain subsidiaries as guarantors. The notes were issued on 2025-08-20 to repay the 6.75% and 9.00% notes, at a charge of USD 23.5 million for call premiums and fee write-offs. The issuer's fair-value estimate for its long-term debt is USD 648.3 million, 96.04% of principal, against 101.14% at the 2025 year-end; that is an estimate, not a quote. The filings report covenant compliance and describe limits on debt, dividends and restricted payments, but print no test levels and do not define the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio, so covenant headroom is not established.

No pension, retiree medical, factoring, supply-chain financing or consent-decree funding was found in the supplied pages. fields.value: Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 11,915 thousand over the last twelve months, 8.19% of Adjusted EBITDA, and in FY2025 the add-backs were USD 39,935 thousand, including USD 13,461 thousand of stock-based compensation and the USD 23,492 thousand debt extinguishment charge. Selling and marketing rose 24.80% over nine months against revenue growth of 15.07%, which the report attributes to the final National Geographic royalty rate step-up and marketing spend, so part of the operating leverage is being absorbed. The last-twelve-month perimeter includes only about two weeks of White Desert and Echo Charlie, whose price is already in cash and debt, so net leverage is conservative against a full-year view that the filings do not give.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions and capital allocation, and governance and disclosure as the eight supplied documents state them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source outside the eight documents was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lindblad is a premium, deposit-funded expedition and land-travel business whose creditors depend on a National Geographic brand license that can end on a change of control, while ownership and board control are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy on the record is neutral to supportive: no dividends have been paid, the 2025 refinancing repaid the earlier notes in full and moved the maturity to 2030, and the preferred stock converted into common stock in February 2026. The leakage to watch is cash spent on acquisitions and on minority interests, which took 56.31% of free cash flow from FY2024 to September 2026, including USD 66.6 million for White Desert and Echo Charlie. A sale of the company, a lost or re-priced license, or a weak booking season would change the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C08; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is premium-priced and sold well ahead, which gives revenue visibility and a deposit float. Guests pay a deposit at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure, and Lindblad segment occupancy rose from 78% in FY2024 to 88% in FY2025 and reached 92% over nine months of 2026, with net yield per available guest night up 14.10% in FY2025. The consequence for creditors is earnings that follow occupancy and price, with cash collected before the voyage that must be delivered afterwards.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration is in a brand and in permits, not in customers. National Geographic can end the brand license, which runs through 2040, on a change of control, on a failure to reach growth or capacity benchmarks by the end of 2032, or on product quality scores, and the royalty is a percentage of ticket revenues with minimums from 2026. The Galápagos vessels operate under permits held on 20-year terms that the government can end early for non-compliance. A lost license or permit would remove the demand channel and the capacity the cash flow relies on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two segments make the earnings, and the land business earns a similar margin on a smaller base. The Lindblad segment was 64.28% of FY2025 tour revenues and Land Experiences 35.72%, while the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.10% and 16.87%. The White Desert and Echo Charlie purchase sits in Land Experiences and adds Antarctic and aviation products, so creditors gain a second profit pool but also integration and provisional-valuation risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C01; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and board control are not established, and that is the main governance gap. The annual report incorporates directors, pay and ownership by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied; what is supplied is a staggered board, anti-takeover provisions, a cap on non-U.S. citizen ownership of 22%, and no dividend policy. No sponsor is identified and no holder above a threshold is named, so conduct is judged from the issuer's actions, not from who owns it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented conduct is creditor-neutral to supportive but cash-hungry. The notes issued in 2025 repaid the 6.75% and 9.00% notes in full and cut the annual coupon cost by USD 1,800 thousand, though principal rose by USD 39,974 thousand to pay premiums and fees. The preferred stock, which ranked ahead of common equity, converted in February 2026. Against that, cash purchases of businesses and minority interests of USD 121,166 thousand since 2024 have used most of the free cash flow, and minority put options remain outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lindb20241231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C07; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is adequate for monitoring. The 2025 statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control, with one critical audit matter on tour revenue recognition, and every quarter states covenant compliance. Comparability is weaker than the opinion suggests, because prior-year captions were reclassified in the 2025 annual report and condensed in the 2026 quarterly reports, and covenant levels are never printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost pressure is in royalties and fuel, and capacity is changing. Lindblad segment fuel expense rose 26.52% over nine months of 2026, the royalty rate has reached its final step-up, two older vessels retire in October 2026, and charter commitments have grown. These raise the cost base that EBITDA must carry before cash interest, so occupancy must keep rising for margins to hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is that the documented conduct is not extractive and the business is performing: occupancy and yield are at their highest in the periods supplied, no dividend has been paid and no stock was bought under the repurchase plan in 2025, the preferred stock is gone, and the notes are not due until September 2030. The view would turn more favourable if a proxy statement showed dispersed ownership, an independent board and no related-party fees, or if the debt documents showed a change-of-control put and tight limits on restricted payments. It would turn adverse if National Geographic amended or ended the license, if a related-party transaction larger than the USD 4.0 million Terra & Tu payment appeared, or if bookings slowed and deposits reversed while acquisition and put-option cash calls continued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the finding that ownership and board control are not established stays open; a concentrated holder, a controlling founder or related-party fees would move the governance view toward higher risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The brand license text is not supplied, so the royalty percentage and the minimum amounts are not stated; this limits how far the license-dependence finding can be turned into a cost or a break-point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Put-option exercise prices are set by fair value at future dates and are not printed; this limits the minority-interest finding to a carrying value and prevents a cash-call estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so any change-of-control put, guarantor list and restricted-payment capacity behind the conduct finding cannot be read; conduct is shown, capacity is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt in the period supplied is the USD 675.0 million of 7.00% senior secured notes due September 2030, issued on 2025-08-20 to prepay the 6.75% and 9.00% notes and to extend the USD 60.0 million revolver to August 2030. No new debt was issued in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 transactions were funded from cash: 60% of White Desert and Echo Charlie for USD 66.6 million on 2026-09-14, with the remaining 40.0% subject to put and call options, and additional stakes in Natural Habitat and Classic Journeys for USD 16.6 million and USD 3.2 million. The preferred stock was converted into common stock on 2026-02-03. A related-party acquisition, Terra & Tu, carries a future payment of up to USD 4.0 million whose date and amount paid are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's overall credit profile, strongest support, primary downside path and monitoring triggers, built on Financial foundation, Business & governance and the eight supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source outside the eight documents was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lindblad's fundamental credit is adequate but thinly covered: net debt is 2.92x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA with no debt principal due before the third quarter of 2030, yet reported EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.32x and liquidity rests on customer deposits that exceed cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is favourable: gross leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 7.68x at FY2025 to 4.97x and free cash flow was USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months. The primary downside path is a booking shortfall that lowers occupancy from the 92% of nine months 2026, reverses deposits and cuts cover, while minority puts, charter commitments and acquisitions keep drawing cash. Covenant levels, ratings and peers are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is earnings-led and has further to run only if earnings hold. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025 and reported EBITDA 54.85% above it, while carrying debt barely moved, so net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 4.70x to 2.92x. The creditor consequence is that the improvement is exposed to any fall in occupancy or price, not locked in by repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is the tightest metric. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x and Adjusted EBITDA 2.52x, and on the 7.00% coupon alone reported EBITDA covers interest 2.83x. The mechanical break-even is large, a 34.51% fall in reported EBITDA before it equals cash interest plus capital spending, but the same earnings reverting to the FY2025 level would put cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C15; calculation C04; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate in size but deposit-funded. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 330,249 thousand compare with unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand, and unrestricted cash is 63.68% of them. Even if every implied cancellable deposit were refunded at once, cash would be USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so the exposure is the speed of deposit reversal, not its size. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand, held as escrow and card-processor reserves, is excluded from the cash used here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is remote before 2030 but unverified after it. The only principal is the 7.00% notes due September 2030, with the revolver ending in August 2030, and the issuer estimates the debt's fair value at 96.04% of principal. Both facilities limit added debt and restricted payments and the issuer reports compliance, but the indenture, credit agreement, guarantors and covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom to add debt or pay out cash is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business has two real concentrations: a brand license and permits. The National Geographic license runs to 2040 but National Geographic can end it early on a change of control, and Galápagos permits run on 20-year terms that can end early for non-compliance. A sale of the company would therefore trigger a credit question that the supplied debt documents cannot answer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is neutral to supportive but cash is going to growth. No dividends were paid, the preferred stock converted, and the 2025 refinancing extended maturities, yet cash purchases of businesses and minority interests used 56.31% of free cash flow from FY2024 to September 2026, and put options remain outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main case for a better view is that earnings are rising, occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026, free cash flow converted 71.82% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months and nothing is due until 2030; even at the FY2025 earnings level, free cash flow was USD 63,838 thousand. The view would improve if reported EBITDA cover rose toward 3x on a stable coupon, if the debt documents showed tight restricted-payment limits and a change-of-control put, and if deposits kept growing alongside cash. It would worsen if occupancy fell back toward the 78% of FY2024, if National Geographic changed the license, if a proxy statement showed concentrated control, or if cash acquisitions kept outrunning free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, ranked first: the earnings base has moved a long way. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025, Lindblad segment occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026 against 78% in FY2024, and net leverage is 2.92x on reported EBITDA. In FY2025 the segment turned each extra dollar of revenue into 28.17% of Adjusted EBITDA against an average margin of 16.10%, so price and occupancy gains reach EBITDA quickly and lower leverage without repayment.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, ranked second: the maturity wall is distant and the creditor group is secured. The 7.00% notes and the revolver are due in 2030 and share first-priority liens on substantially all assets, so there is no principal to refinance for almost four years and the secured claim sits over the ship fleet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, ranked third: cash generation is positive after capital spending. Free cash flow was USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months and 14.44% of carrying debt, which supports gradual debt reduction if acquisitions slow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, ranked first: cover is thin for a discretionary, season-dependent business. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x, and cover was 1.70x in FY2025, so a moderate earnings fall quickly absorbs the margin of safety.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, ranked second: liquidity depends on customer deposits and is not covenant-tested here. Unrestricted cash is 63.68% of unearned passenger revenues and the revolver is undrawn but unread, so a booking shock would draw cash before revenue falls.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, ranked third: dependence on a brand license and permits, with control and covenant facts missing. The license can end on a change of control, the Galápagos permits can end early, and the proxy statement and debt documents are not supplied, so the creditor cannot see who controls the company or what it may pay out.

fields.value: Figures stated in the sources and used in the narrative sections below:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lindblad sells premium expedition cruises on owned small ships and land-based adventure travel, with deposits paid at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure. That gives revenue visibility about nine months ahead and a deposit float, which supports debt service when bookings hold but turns into a refund and cash-timing risk if they fall. The Lindblad segment was 64.28% of FY2025 tour revenues and Land Experiences 35.72%, so the ship business sets the credit and the land brands add diversification at a similar Adjusted EBITDA margin (16.10% against 16.87%). Recent history is acquisitive: the Thomson Group in 2024, Torcatt in 2025 and White Desert and Echo Charlie in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-31_lindb20241231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lindblad is a listed Delaware company with a founder as board co-chair, no identified sponsor and no holder above a threshold is named; the proxy statement is not supplied. The group holds controlling stakes in Natural Habitat, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine and Classic Journeys, and since September 2026 in White Desert and Echo Charlie, with minority put and call options, and the notes and revolver are guaranteed by the Company and certain subsidiaries that are not listed. A board divided into three classes, a charter limit of 22% on non-U.S. citizen ownership that lets the company redeem excess shares, and a Coastwise Laws limit of 24.99% for the entities that own U.S.-flagged vessels all limit takeovers and equity sales. Financial policy is judged from conduct, which is neutral to supportive, because control cannot be read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is premium-priced and discretionary. Net yield per available guest night rose 14.10% in FY2025 and occupancy from 78% to 88%, and 92% over nine months of 2026, but in past recessions occupancy and pricing fell, and about 90% of expedition guest ticket revenue comes from U.S. guests. Direct sales are 69.97% of Lindblad guest ticket revenue over nine months of 2026, which gives control of pricing and deposits but concentrates marketing cost. Revenue is therefore visible for the booked season and cyclical beyond it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C06; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are expanding but the cost base is exposed to royalties and fuel. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 16.37% in FY2025 to 16.93% over the last twelve months, helped because cost of tours fell from 52.50% of tour revenues over nine months of 2025 to 51.05% in 2026 and general and administrative expense grew 3.40% against tour revenue growth of 15.07%, which shows operating leverage; selling and marketing rose 24.80% on the final royalty step-up and marketing, and Lindblad fuel expense rose 26.52%. Fuel is a modest and generally unhedged cost, 3.1% of tour revenues in FY2025 against 4.9% in FY2023, while currency exposure is partly hedged. Fixed and variable cost are not split, so resilience under a volume fall is not established beyond the FY2025 and FY2024 comparison.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C08; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is moderate and fell in 2026: 3.47% of last-twelve-month tour revenues against 6.19% in FY2025, a year that included the refurbishment of two recently acquired Galápagos vessels. Free cash flow converted 71.82% of reported EBITDA, helped by deposit growth that supplied 30.90% of operating cash flow. Cash interest on the notes is paid on March 15 and September 15, and the maintenance and growth split of capital spending is not stated, so the durable level of free cash flow is below the reported figure by the deposit contribution and by any acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate and rising: the market is fragmented among private operators and the company expects large cruise operators to enter through acquisitions and new vessels. Entry barriers appear meaningful on analyst inference from permits, ship lead times and remote-operations experience, which helps pricing but does not stop well-funded entrants. Land-based and other premium travel are substitutes for discretionary spending. Buyer power is limited by direct sales, but travel agents and wholesalers supplied about 32% of expedition guest ticket revenue in FY2025. Supplier power sits with shipyards, fuel, charter owners and the National Geographic license, which carries a change-of-control termination right.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and economics matter to credit; social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver. Regulatory exposure is the Coastwise Laws and ownership cap, Galápagos permit terms, Federal Maritime Commission certification backed by a passenger-deposit escrow account, and emissions rules; economic exposure is discretionary demand from affluent U.S. travellers, fuel and interest rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: premium pricing and high occupancy; distant 2030 maturity with secured status; positive free cash flow; non-extractive conduct record.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaknesses: thin interest cover; deposit-funded liquidity; dependence on one brand license and permits; negative book equity and a working-capital deficit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opportunities that improve credit: continued price and occupancy gains; integration of White Desert and Echo Charlie; lower capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats that weaken credit: travel or economic shocks; fuel and royalty costs; a change of control; further cash acquisitions and put exercises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are adequate: tour revenues of USD 859,592 thousand over the last twelve months with a premium niche. The competitive advantage rests on brand and permits and is conditional on the license. Diversification is moderate: two segments and eight brands, but the Lindblad ship segment supplied 63.19% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA. Cost and capex flexibility is moderate, margins are improving but exposed to royalty and fuel, free cash flow is positive but deposit-aided, ability to refinance is helped by the 2030 maturity but unverified without the documents, liquidity is adequate in size but deposit-funded, and financial policy and governance cannot be assessed beyond conduct. The trend is improving, the main constraint is 2.32x cover, and the key missing data are the debt documents, the proxy statement and any peer or rating reference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For FY2026 the company guides tour revenues of USD 870 million to USD 885 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 142 million to USD 148 million. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is already USD 131,407 thousand, so the guidance implies a fourth quarter of USD 10,593 thousand to USD 16,593 thousand against USD 14,150 thousand in the fourth quarter of 2025: no further step up is guided, and it is not stated whether that reflects caution or the October 2026 retirement of two vessels. Tailwinds are pricing, occupancy above 90% and lower capital spending; headwinds are the royalty step-up, fuel, the retirement of two vessels in October 2026 and more charter commitments. Over three to five years industry forecasts cited by the company point to growing ship-based travel, which supports demand but also draws new competitors; the debt is due in 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a shock to travel demand, such as a geopolitical event, a weather or ship incident or an economic downturn; past recessions lowered occupancy and pricing. The first operational break is bookings: fewer new deposits and some cancellations lower revenue visibility, and Lindblad segment Adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 20,375 thousand when occupancy rose 10 percentage points and price improved in FY2025, so a comparable reversal would remove a similar amount. On the financial side, earnings returning to the FY2025 level would leave cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x with the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, yet FY2025 itself produced positive free cash flow. On liquidity, refunding every implied cancellable deposit would still leave cash of USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x the calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so a deposit reversal alone would not cause liquidity distress within the 2027 fixed charges, and cash alone would cover them 1.40x. Management levers are lower capital spending, slower acquisitions and puts, and fewer discretionary costs; the observable triggers are occupancy, the deposit balance relative to cash, and cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation C06; calculation C03; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Lindblad presents an adequate business profile supported by premium pricing, high occupancy and a secured 2030 maturity, but credit quality is constrained by thin cover, deposit-funded liquidity, brand and permit dependence and cash used on acquisitions. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to positive free cash flow after capital spending and no principal before 2030, although part of the free cash flow comes from deposit growth that can reverse. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings staying above the FY2025 level, on revolver availability and on the change-of-control terms. The primary downside path is a booking shortfall that lowers occupancy and deposits while ship, royalty, charter and coupon costs continue, cutting cover from 2.32x and drawing cash that deposits had pre-funded. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the proxy statement, the brand license terms, the put-option prices and a peer set, because the comparison with other leveraged issuers in the sector is not established. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: loss of earnings coverage through a booking shortfall.
